newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MILAN'S DREAMS OF SIXTH CUP BLOWN AWAY BY ROSENBORG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN'S DREAMS OF SIXTH CUP BLOWN AWAY BY ROSENBORG.

text.p: AC Milan's dreams of lifting the European Cup for a record-equalling sixth time were blown away on Wednesday by Norway's Rosenborg Trondheim, who went to the San Siro needing nothing less than victory and beat the Italians 2-1.
While Milan made a surprise exit, two famous clubs who had looked seriously threatened -- Ajax Amsterdam and Manchester United -- pulled off away wins to reach the European Cup quarter-finals.
Milan, back under the guidance of Arrigo Sacchi who resigned as manager of Italy on Sunday, only needed a point against a side little-known outside their home country before this season.

But they fell behind when Harald Brattbakk scored after 29 minutes and lost the match to a 69th minute winner from Vegard Heggem after Milan's French international Christophe Dugarry had equalised on the stroke of half-time.
It was an astonishing defeat for the Italians, the most successful club side in Europe over the past decade, who were looking to equal Real Madrid's 30-year-old record of six European Cup triumphs.
Milan had beaten the Norwegians 4-1 in Scandinavia earlier in the competition and, despite a poor run in Serie A, had always been favourites to qualify from group D with Porto.
The result marks a dreadful return to the club for Sacchi, who twice steered the side to the European Cup in 1989 and 1990.

It also deprives the competition of what would have been a fascinating all-Italian quarter-final in March between Milan, who have appeared in five of the last eight European Cup finals, and newly-crowned world club champions Juventus.
Instead, Juventus meet Rosenborg, who will be hoping for another sensational performance against an Italian side to propel them, against all odds, into the last four.
Milan's high-profile owner Silvio Berlusconi, who took over as president in 1986, said the defeat was "the lowest point in our luck and in the league since I have been at Milan."
"I'm disappointed and saddened," the billionaire media mogul and former prime minister said. "But we have to learn from it and rebuild. We will do it with the right leader (Sacchi)."
While Milan were floundering, European pedigree was asserting itself elsewhere on the continent.

Ajax Amsterdam, bidding for their third consecutive European Cup final but needing an away win from their final Champions' League game to qualify from group A, pulled out the stops to beat Grasshopper Zurich 1-0 in Switzerland.

And Manchester United, lying third in group C before start of play, defeated Rapid Vienna 2-0 on a chilly night in Austria and had Juventus to thank for snuffing out Fenerbahce's quarter-final hopes by beating the Turks by the same scoreline in Turin.
Patrick Kluivert scored Ajax's vital goal after 31 minutes to keep alive the Dutch champions' remarkable away record in European competition.
Other than last season's European Cup final against Juventus in Rome where they were defeated on penalties, Ajax have not lost a European tie outside Amsterdam for the past three seasons.

The result was a bitter blow for Grasshopper, who led group A for the first four games of the competition but who paid the price on Wednesday for their surprise 2-1 reverse against strugglers Glasgow Rangers three weeks ago.
Ajax qualify in second place, level on points with European Cup debutants Auxerre, who clinched their quarter-final berth on Wednesday with a 2-1 victory over Rangers in France.
The French champions now meet Borussia Dortmund, who finished runners-up in group B despite winning their final match against Steaua Bucharest 5-3.
Ajax meet group B winners Atletico Madrid, who beat Widzew Lodz 1-0 in their final group fixture.

Manchester United, reeling after two consecutive 1-0 European home defeats before Wednesday, finally rediscovered their ability to score against Rapid, who exited the competition as the only side without a victory to their name.

Ryan Giggs and Eric Cantona found the net for the English champions, whose fans spent as much time listening out for the score from Turin as watching their own side's level-headed performance in sub-zero temperatures in the Austrian capital.

If Fenerbahce had beaten Juventus, United's win would not have been enough to take them through. In the event, goals from Michele Padovano and Nicola Amoruso gave Juve victory and calmed English nerves.
United meet group D winners Porto in the quarter-finals. The Portuguese champions chalked up their fifth Champions' League victory in six games by beating Gothenburg 2-0 in Sweden.

Wednesday's results mean seven of the eight pre-tournament favourites have survived the group phase. The only absentees will be Milan, the overall favourites before the first group matches way back in September.
Juventus were quoted by British bookmakers Ladbrokes as 11-8 favourites to defend their title after Wednesday's matches Rosenborg, the team they face next, were ranked as 50-1 outsiders.
